text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: Add InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler to EXCAVA’s pipeline first. It regenerates detail in low-res frames without blurring edges, which directly boosts reconstruction quality—even a 0.5% gain here compounds across long videos. The trade-off is compute: it needs a GPU with VRAM for real-time upscaling, but the model’s lightweight design keeps the hit under 15% compared to baseline.

name: Torque
text: InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler won’t fix EXCAVA’s face fidelity drop because it targets *geometry*, not identity—faces blur or distort when the base model’s reconstruction is weak. A better move is testing RealVisXL’s face model in the pipeline first; if it locks identity but still fails on full-frame distortion, we’ll know the bottleneck is reconstruction, not detail. Settle it by running a blind A/B test: compare EXCAVA’s output with and without RealVisXL’s face model, then measure face similarity scores and full-frame distortion metrics.

name: Gearbox
text:
Add RealVisXL v1.1’s face model to EXCAVA’s pipeline first. It locks facial identity better than any other open model, which cuts the biggest failure mode in reconstruction—faces turning into strangers. The trade-off is compute: RealVisXL’s face model needs a dedicated GPU slot, but the identity stability alone justifies the cost.

name: Torque
text: RealVisXL’s face model locks identity but won’t fix EXCAVA’s full-frame distortion—it only patches one symptom. The real risk is wasting compute on a partial fix while the core reconstruction model (likely weak on geometry) still fails. Test RealVisXL *only* if we first verify the base model’s face fidelity with a controlled clip; if faces distort there, no face model saves it.

name: Dynamo
text: DECISION: Add RealVisXL v1.1’s face model to EXCAVA’s pipeline first, then layer InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler only if face fidelity holds but geometry still drops—own the integration and benchmark the compounded quality gain.
